sections.label: Workgroup retirement age recommendations
sections.summary: The Workgroup recommended raising retirement and re-employment ages by three years to 65 and 70 by the end of the decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Workgroup went on to recommend increasing both the retirement age and re-employment age by three years to 65 and 70, respectively, by the end of the decade.

sections.label: Government accepts recommendations
sections.summary: The Government has accepted all of these recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Government has accepted all of these recommendations.

sections.label: Statutory retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: The Government will prescribe the statutory retirement age and re-employment age to be 63 and 68 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In line with the consensus of the tripartite partners, the Government will prescribe the statutory retirement age and re-employment age to be 63 and 68 respectively.

sections.label: Senior workers CPF contribution increase
sections.summary: The first increase in senior workers' CPF contribution rate takes effect from 1 January 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In particular, the first increase in senior workers' CPF contribution rate will take effect from 1 January 2022.

sections.label: Senior Worker Support Package offsets
sections.summary: The Government introduced the $1.5 billion Senior Worker Support Package in 2020, providing offsets for senior workers' wages and additional employer CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Government is also doing our part to help employers adjust to these changes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We introduced the $1.5 billion Senior Worker Support Package in 2020 and, through this package, we provide offsets for senior workers' wages and the additional employer CPF contributions.

sections.label: Streaming out CPF account savings
sections.summary: The Ordinary and Special Account savings of these members will be automatically streamed out by the first quarter of next year, benefiting about 83,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To minimise the disruption to payouts, we will automatically stream out the Ordinary and Special Account savings of these members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This change will take effect by the first quarter of next year and will benefit about 83,000 members.

sections.label: Silver Support payouts and deferral
sections.summary: About 250,000 seniors aged 65 and above will benefit from Silver Support payouts in 2021, up from 150,000, and deferring payouts can raise them by up to 7% per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As a result, almost 250,000 seniors aged 65 and above will benefit from Silver Support payouts in 2021, and this is up from 150,000 previously.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Members who choose to defer the start of payouts can benefit from payouts that are up to 7% higher for each year deferred.

sections.label: Retirement Sum Topping-Up top-ups
sections.summary: In 2020, top-ups via the Retirement Sum Topping-Up scheme reached about $3 billion across 140,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The year 2020 saw a record amount of top-ups via the Retirement Sum Topping-Up scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This amounts to about $3 billion across 140,000 members.

sections.label: CPF cash top-up tax relief
sections.summary: From 1 January 2022, the annual tax relief cap for cash top-ups rises to $8,000 for one's own CPF accounts and another $8,000 for loved ones, up from $7,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: From 1 January 2022, givers can also look forward to an annual tax relief cap of $8,000 when they make cash top-ups to their own CPF accounts and another $8,000 when they do so for their loved ones, up from $7,000.

sections.label: Disbursement of deceased members' CPF
sections.summary: With improved automatic disbursement arrangements, about 93% of deceased members have their nominated CPF monies fully disbursed within six months of death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With the improvements in automatic disbursement arrangements, about 93% of deceased members have their nominated CPF monies fully disbursed within six months of death.

sections.label: Shortening unclaimed CPF retention period
sections.summary: The retention period for unclaimed CPF monies will be shortened from seven years to six months after the Board is notified of the member's death, with no interest payable after transfer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Given these developments and the convenience of automatic disbursement, there is no longer a need to allow for the retention of unclaimed CPF monies over such a long period of time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will, therefore, shorten this duration from seven years, to six months after the Board is notified of the member’s death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Should a nominee choose not to make claims within six months, the monies will be transferred out of the deceased member’s CPF accounts, and no interest will be payable from then.

sections.label: New durations start date
sections.summary: The new durations will apply from 1 April 2022 to give some transition time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The new durations will apply from 1 April 2022, to give some transition time.

sections.label: CPF monies to beneficiaries
sections.summary: Over the last five years, about 98% of CPF monies have been distributed to beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In fact, over the last five years, about 98% of CPF monies have been distributed to beneficiaries.

sections.label: Recovering grants from members
sections.summary: Amendments will be made to streamline how the Government recovers grants from members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Second, amendments will be made to streamline how the Government recovers grants from members.

sections.label: Matched Retirement Savings Scheme grant recovery
sections.summary: The amendment lets the CPF Board recover the accompanying grant if reversal appeals are approved case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) was launched in 2021 to encourage top-ups to eligible seniors with lower balances by providing one-for-one Government matching for eligible top-ups up to $600 per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: However, a minority of members may choose to appeal for such reversals despite knowing that the accompanying grant will also be reversed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This amendment allows the CPF Board to recover the accompanying grant should such appeals be approved on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Amendments for retirement payouts
sections.summary: The amendments help members build retirement nest eggs and receive payouts smoothly while streamlining CPF scheme administration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The various amendments will help members build up their retirement nest eggs and receive retirement payouts smoothly while streamlining administration of CPF schemes.

sections.label: Rising life expectancy
sections.summary: Life expectancy continues to rise, from about 78 years old 20 years ago to 84 years old today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: First, our life expectancy continues to rise, from about 78 years old 20 years ago to 84 years old today and is expected to continue to rise.

sections.label: Employers and experienced workers
sections.summary: Employers can tap a wider manpower pool to employ experienced workers, and the Bill legalises and operationalises these trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Second, employers can also tap on a wider manpower pool available to continue employing experienced workers to cope with the current manpower crunch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This is also the main objective of the Bill today, which is to legalise and operationalise the implications brought forth by these two trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The most important thing is to give employees appropriate legal protection so that they can remain in the workforce until the statutory retirement age.

sections.label: Retirement age and CPF confusion
sections.summary: The speaker says debating both Bills together may confuse the public into linking retirement age with CPF withdrawal age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I think this is important, especially for today's Second Reading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We are debating both Bills together and members of the public may be confused and think that could be linked together: retirement age and your CPF withdrawal age.

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: The Bill enables the Government to raise the minimum retirement age from 62 to 65 and re-employment age from 67 to 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The intent of this Bill as I understand it is to enable the Government to raise the minimum retirement age and re-employment ages by the year 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The minimum retirement age will go up progressively from 62 to 65 while the re-employment age will be raised progressively from 67 to 70.

sections.label: Singapore life expectancy figures
sections.summary: A 2019 review states Singaporeans' life expectancy is 81.4 years for men and 85.7 years for women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a 2019 Singapore Public Sector Outcomes Review, Singaporeans' life expectancy is among the highest in the world at 81.4 years for men and 85.7 years for women.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination guidelines becoming law
sections.summary: At the National Day Rally, the Prime Minister announced workplace anti-discrimination guidelines would be enshrined into law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At this year's National Day Rally, the Prime Minister announced that workplace anti-discrimination guidelines would be enshrined into law.

sections.label: Retirement and Re-employment Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to raise retirement and re-employment ages to 65 and 70 by 2030, starting 1 July 2022 at 63 and 68.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Retirement and Re-employment (Amendment) Bill seeks to raise the retirement age and re-employment ages in Singapore to 65 years and 70 years respectively by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The first move is to commence from 1 July 2022, increasing the retirement and re-employment ages to 63 and 68 respectively.

sections.label: Reviewing one-off payment amount
sections.summary: It is submitted the one-off payment of 3.5 months' salary, minimum S$5,500 and maximum S$13,000, needs review and increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, with the increase in median wages and the cost of living in Singapore, it is submitted that the existing one-off payment equivalent to 3.5 months' salary, subject to a minimum of S$5,500 and maximum of S$13,000, needs to be reviewed and increased.

sections.label: Salary support for mature PMEs
sections.summary: The Government could consider short-term salary support of up to 50%, capped at S$3,800 monthly for six months, for companies hiring unemployed mature PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To assist mature PMEs, the Government could consider providing a short-term salary support, for example, up to 50% salary funding, capped at S$3,800 per month for six months, for companies who hire mature PMEs who are unemployed, to lower the cost and risk for companies to hire this group of PMEs with relevant skills.

sections.label: Justifying changes to re-employment terms
sections.summary: Employers could be required to justify in writing material changes in re-employment terms or sudden lack of internal vacancies for older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Bearing in mind that older workers have performed satisfactorily and been employed in that role over the years, we could require employers to justify in writing, inter alia, any material changes in the re-employment terms of older workers and/or sudden lack of internal vacancies for the said role, when these employees have been employed in that role over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This is to avoid a situation whereby companies unilaterally offer significant pay cuts or reduction of employment benefits to the mature worker, under the guise of having re-negotiated the employment terms with the mature worker, while expecting the same standards and deliverables from the mature worker.

sections.label: CAYE Scheme for self-employed persons
sections.summary: The Contribute-As-You-Earn Scheme helps self-employed persons contribute to MediSave as they earn, and currently applies only to public sector contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The "Contribute-As-You-Earn" Scheme, the "CAYE Scheme" for short, helps self-employed persons, SEPs for short, contribute to their MediSave as they earn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At present, the CAYE Scheme is only applicable to public sector contracts.

sections.label: Service buyer CPF contributions for SEPs
sections.summary: The speaker proposes service buyers from public and private sectors make additional CPF contributions for SEPs, mirroring employer contributions, and makes three suggestions for MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: What I am proposing is one step further, that the service buyers from both the public sector and private sector, make additional contributions to the SEP's CPF account; which mirrors the employer's CPF contributions under normal employment relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: If accepted, this would mean that practically, service buyers would be making CPF contributions consisting of both the SEP's portion under the existing CAYE scheme, as well as additional sums being the service buyer’s contributions too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Amidst the pandemic, I am heartened that our Government has chosen to stay the course and continue with the planned increase of retirement age from 62 to 63, and re-employment age from 67 to 68.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Beyond adjusting the re-employment and retirement age, I also like to make three suggestions for MOM to improve our senior’s livelihood and retirement adequacy, namely: increasing our seniors’ CPF contribution rate, fighting ageism through the upcoming anti-discrimination legislations and exploring new ways of helping seniors above 60 to find and hold on to jobs.

sections.label: Raising senior CPF contribution rates
sections.summary: The Government could push for higher CPF contribution rates for all seniors after broad economic recovery and add anti-ageism clauses to upcoming anti-discrimination legislations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One way that the Government can consider doing, to balance both the interest of both our senior workers and our struggling sectors, is to: push for the contribution rate for all seniors to increase, as long as the broad majority of our economy has made a recovery, and encourage the National Wage Council to adopt even more overall wage flexibility depending on the performance of the sector and the firm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: My second point is that I hope the Government can put in anti-ageism clauses in the upcoming anti-discrimination legislations.

sections.label: Raising re-employment age to 70
sections.summary: The amendments propose raising the re-employment age to 70 and providing additional modest protection for dismissals on grounds of retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Once we get past this stabilisation phase, which we will, we must step up more to increase our seniors' employability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can consider the ideas raised and start preparing for that day.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The amendments tabled this time propose to further raise the re-employment age to 70, while affording some additional modest protection for dismissals on the grounds of retirement age.

sections.label: Older Singaporeans by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, close to a million Singaporeans will be aged 65 or older.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: By 2030, the number of Singaporeans, aged 65 or older, will be close to a million.

sections.label: Freedom to work at advanced age
sections.summary: This calls for permitting workers to choose to work at any advanced age if able, willing and able to secure a job.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Rather, this is a call to permit workers the freedom to continue to choose to work at any advanced age as long as they are able and willing to and are able to secure a job.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination laws and retirement age
sections.summary: Evidence shows anti-discrimination laws boost older worker employment, making abolition of the retirement age an essential complement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, there is evidence that anti-discrimination laws have been effective at boosting the employment of older workers, to the extent that we subscribe to non-discrimination in the workplace; then, the abolition of the retirement age is an essential complement to a richer set of legislative provisions to that effect.

sections.label: Workers' Party lowering retirement age
sections.summary: The Workers' Party has repeatedly called for lowering this age to 60, decoupling retirement from retirement savings decisions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Workers' Party has also repeatedly called for the lowering of this age to 60.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This amounts to decoupling the retirement decision from the retirement savings decision.

sections.label: Voluntary withdrawals and minimum retirement age
sections.summary: Delayed withdrawals should be voluntary; the Bill lets the Minister set a minimum retirement age of at least 62 but not more than 65.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Regardless, such delayed withdrawals should be a purely voluntary scheme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Taken together, Mr Speaker, these changes will permit our people to exercise far greater agency, individual self-responsibility and freedom to choose their desired course of employment in their senior years as well as weigh their various retirement options in an informed and unconstrained manner.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is something that all in this House would wish for those who have blazed the trail before us and for this reason, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill empowers the Minister to specify the prescribed minimum retirement age applicable to any class of employees who must be at least 62 years but not more than 65.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employers cannot dismiss the employees on the ground of age before they reach the prescribed minimum retirement age.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup older worker recommendations
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers recommended raising retirement and re-employment ages to 65 and 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers recommended that the retirement age and re-employment age be raised to 65 and 70 respectively by 2030, with the first increases to 62 and 68 in 2022.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age changes
sections.summary: The prescribed retirement and re-employment ages in legislation will likely need to change to reflect people's preferences.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is a very good thing, however, people finally make their choices.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is likely that the prescribed retirement age and re-employment age encapsulated in our legislation will need to change to reflect people's preferences.

sections.label: Report recommendations and two Bills
sections.summary: Two Bills give legislative effect to recommendations raising retirement age, re-employment age and CPF contribution rates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Report itself contained 22 recommendations and, of the 22, the three most prominent recommendations pertained to the progressive raising of the statutory retirement age from 62 to 65 by the end of the decade, the corresponding raising of the re-employment age ceiling from 67 to 70 over that same timeframe, and also the progressive improvement of CPF contribution rates for both employers and employees for workers aged 55 to 70.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The two Bills before us today, the Retirement and Re-employment (Amendment) Bill as well as the Central Provident Fund (Amendment) Bill, they are to give legislative effect to these recommendations so that they can be implemented to the benefit of both workers and companies.

sections.label: COVID-19 delays CPF rate increase
sections.summary: Tripartite partners delayed the CPF rate increase to January 2022 but kept the July 2022 retirement and re-employment age increases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It affects the lives of our people, it effects the livelihoods of our older workers and their retirement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: That was to be followed by the increase in the retirement and re-employment ages by one year each in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: But as we know, last year, COVID-19 hit us.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As a result, the tripartite partners discussed how do we do this in a way that does not derail the entire intent, but take into account the serious circumstances that we have to face.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And as a result, we agreed to delay the implementation of the increase of the CPF rates by a year, hence, January 2022, but to keep in place the planned increased in the re-employment and retirement ages in July 2022.

sections.label: Transition offset package for CPF
sections.summary: The Government will consider a transition offset for part of the cost employees bear when CPF contribution rates increase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It is with regard the transition offset package.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This was mentioned in previous speeches that when you increase the CPF contribution rates, that Government will consider a transition offset for part of the cost that the employees would have to bear.

sections.label: Employment rate for older workers
sections.summary: MOM figures show the employment rate for workers 65 and older rose slightly in 2020 compared to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In fact, according to figures released by MOM, the employment rate for workers 65 years and older actually showed a small increase in the year 2020, compared to the year 2019.

sections.label: Anxiety over job insecurity
sections.summary: A report recently submitted to the Government shows palpable anxiety over job insecurity among those aged 40 to 60.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Their report was recently submitted to the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It is clear from the report that the anxiety over job insecurity among those aged 40 to 60 is palpable.

sections.label: Mature workforce retraining capacity
sections.summary: The growing mature local workforce requires checking whether current retraining, career guidance and job matching mechanisms have the capacity and speed to handle heavier loads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must recognise that the size of the mature local workforce will grow rapidly in the coming years because of demography and changes in the business environment will only accelerate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must consider whether our current mechanisms in facilitating retraining and career guidance and job matching on an individual, inter-company as well as inter-industry transfer level, do we actually have anticipated capacity and effectiveness, the swiftness of that switching to tackle the heavier loads that we can anticipate that are oncoming.

sections.label: Social support for income breaks
sections.summary: We must review and strengthen social support to target income breaks and reduce the cost of retraining, job search and job conversion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And the latter, if that happens, will come back to haunt society in weakened retirement adequacy and frayed social fabric.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Thus, we must review and strengthen the social support to target the breaks in income that will inevitably affect more people and reduce the cost of their active retraining, job search and job conversion.

sections.label: Structured guidance for mature workers
sections.summary: The fragmented landscape needs more structure, anchoring, shared services and periodic check-ins to produce last mile outcomes for mature workers from their 40s.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The current operating landscape may be too fragmented and cannot offer pervasive and sound guidance that links training to ops, future planning in companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, more structure, more anchoring, consideration of shared services and periodic check-ins at the company and individual levels – as Minister has also alluded to just now – in terms of what you should be doing with your mature workers, would be needed to produce the required last mile outcomes for the majority of mature workers, starting in their 40s.

sections.label: Tying policies and implementation together
sections.summary: Success requires tying policies, resourcing, partnerships and implementation more tightly together, beyond extending working ages by law or wage subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: To do so successfully, we must not only extend the working ages by law or help make hiring cost-effective through wage subsidies – though these are important – but we must also tie our policies, resourcing, partnerships and implementation more tightly together.

sections.label: Employer misconception on retirement age
sections.summary: An employer telling a resident they are too near retirement age wrongly suggests the law prevents employment beyond the statutory retirement age, which is false.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: So, it is that way and not the other way.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: So, in that particular example that was cited, for that employer to tell Assoc Prof Lim's resident that, "Actually, I would like to employ you but, you know, you are too near the retirement age", would suggest that the employer is actually saying that, "Well, I am prevented by law from employing you beyond the statutory retirement age" which is false.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: So, I hope that we should also make this point very, very clear to employers and to workers.

sections.label: CPF disbursements for significant condition
sections.summary: Clause 4 section 15AA allows CPF automatic disbursements for a specified significant condition, raising questions on the condition and social assistance eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under clause 4 section 15AA, allowing CPF to make automatic disbursements to the member if he or she is suffering from a specified significant condition.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: First, can more details be shared on the significant condition that entails this exception?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Second, if the member is currently covered under a social assistance programme, will the CPF disbursement impact his or her eligibility from continued assistance under the current social assistance scheme?

sections.label: CPF nomination rates
sections.summary: Only more than two in five CPF members have made a nomination, with those aged 65 and above higher at three in four.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: As in February this year, it was just shared that only more than two in five CPF members have made a nomination with those among 65 and above higher at three in four having done so.

sections.label: Older jobseekers coaching outcomes
sections.summary: Of 34,000 jobseekers who sought career coaching in 2020, 60% were above 40, and four in 10 of these found no job within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Among the 34,000 jobseekers who sought career coaching help from Workforce Singapore and the Employment and Employability Institute in 2020, 60% were above the age of 40 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Of these, four out of 10 were unable to find jobs within six months.

sections.label: Senior employment schemes and rates
sections.summary: Schemes including the Senior Employment Credit and others have helped keep employment rates at over 67% for ages 55 to 64 and 28.5% for those above 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Schemes such as the Senior Employment Credit, the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant, the Part-time Re-employment Grant and the CPF Transition Grant have helped to keep the employment rate of those aged 55 to 64 years old at over 67% and the employment rate of those above 65 at 28.5%.

sections.label: CPF LIFE and retiree households
sections.summary: CPF LIFE gives monthly payouts to seniors beyond 65, but a 2019 survey found retiree households in public flats need more than CPF payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This reflects the strength of our CPF system, particularly the CPF LIFE scheme which ensures that seniors beyond the age of 65 will receive a monthly payout no matter how long they live.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, the latest Household Expenditure Survey conducted in 2019 found that retiree households living in public flats require more than just their CPF payouts and most receive money from their children and family members.

sections.label: Ageing population and retirement age
sections.summary: An ageing population, declining fertility and rising life expectancies tighten the labour market, and the speaker supports raising the statutory retirement and re-employment ages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is faced with an increasingly tight labour market due to the rapidly ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, coupled with a shrinking working-age population caused by Singapore’s declining fertility trend which hit a low of 1.1 resident TFR in 2020, will further exacerbate our tight labour market situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Life expectancies have risen to such levels that many people think that they do not have sufficient savings to meet post-retirement living and healthcare expenses, and therefore want the option to work for longer so as to improve their financial adequacy for retirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the raising of the statutory retirement age and re-employment age, and that our senior workers have the option to stay employed longer if they so choose.

sections.label: Off-ramp programme for older employees
sections.summary: The speaker advocates companies begin a gentle five-year off-ramp programme for employees between 55 and 65, maybe even 70.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Apparently, this is a travel industry term indicating the time between the high and low travel seasons of a specific destination between the peak and off-peak months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I advocate that companies begin a gentle off-ramp programme spread over five years for their employees between 55 and 65 – maybe even 70.

sections.label: Senior Worker Support Package grants
sections.summary: Companies lacking systems to execute appreciate the Senior Worker Support Package and Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant, which help companies enhance HR policies for re-employment of mature workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many companies, however, do not have the systems and capabilities to execute and are, therefore, very appreciative of the Government's Senior Worker Support Package and the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant, which are targeted to help companies accelerate enhancement of their company HR policies to support re-employment of mature workers for both full-time and part-time work.

sections.label: Ageism and mid-career transition
sections.summary: The speaker advocates mid-career transition programmes for staff aged 45 to 55 and notes some Singapore companies already have HR policies supporting mature workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, we should look out for ageism mindset not to set in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am also advocating that our tripartite partners and companies provide a different kind of career counselling and coaching for their staff aged between 45 and 55 years of age during the pre-retirement phase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At this stage of their life, they ought to be enrolled into a mid-career transition programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This programme should provide the workers with mid-career strategies to help them think about their physical health and financial health, adequacy for retirement, think about their strengths and what keeps them motivated, think about their skills gaps for future jobs with the company or the industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is heartwarming for me to know, when I spoke to quite a few HR officers, that there are a good number of Singapore companies which already, on their own, have HR policies that support keeping their mature workers for as long as they are healthy, able, positive-minded and willing to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These companies find that mature workers who have been with the company for more than 10 to 15 years are more loyal, job hop less, are more appreciative of having the opportunity to work and more productive because of their experience and skills built up over the years.

sections.label: Clause 50 unnominated monies amendments
sections.summary: Clause 50 amendments allow the Public Trustee flexibility to disburse unnominated monies on a member's death, including funeral expenses and payments to a beneficiary representative.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From this perspective, the amendments proposed by clause 50 of the Bill, which allow for greater flexibility and efficiency for disbursement of unnominated monies in the event of a member's death are welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These changes allow the Public Trustee to reimburse reasonable funeral expenses incurred by a beneficiary out of the unnominated monies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It also allows the Public Trustee to pay a sum of money up to a specified limit to be released directly to a beneficiary representative for disbursement in accordance with intestacy laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would it be an amount that changes like the Retirement Sum Scheme?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We also welcome the removal of the ceiling for voluntary contributions to MediSave.

sections.label: Question on unchanged amendments
sections.summary: The passage asks whether this remains unchanged with the amendments being proposed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Does this remain unchanged with the amendments being proposed?

sections.label: Population above 65 projections
sections.summary: In 2020, 15.2% of the population was above 65, and by 2030 more than 20% is projected to be 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2020, 15.2% of our population is above 65 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: By 2030, it is projected that more than 20% of our population will be 65 years old and above.

sections.label: Employer CPF contribution rate age
sections.summary: The speaker proposes reducing the employer's CPF contribution rate only at 60 years old, not 55, and asks MOM and the Tripartite Workgroup to consider this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, it is arbitrary to start reducing the employer’s CPF contribution rate at 55 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I propose that MOM and the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers consider, at the right time and, hopefully, earlier, to reduce the employer’s CPF contribution rate only at 60 years old and not 55 years old.

sections.label: Taxi drivers retirement age increase
sections.summary: A request for the Government to consider progressively raising taxi drivers' retirement age to 78 from 75 to create more jobs for those above 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As part of the efforts to create more jobs for those above 70 years old, I would like the Government to consider increasing the retirement age of taxi drivers to 78 years old progressively, up from the current 75.

sections.label: Ageing population projections
sections.summary: In 2010, 9% of the population was aged 65 and above, projected to exceed 20% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2010, 9% of our population was aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: By 2030, it is projected that more than 20% of our population will be 65 years old and above.

sections.label: Taxi safety features and retirement age
sections.summary: Citing automatic emergency brake and lane departure alert in many taxis, a call to raise taxi drivers' retirement age to 78 with yearly health checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Many taxis are equipped with automatic emergency brake and lane departure alert.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Government to raise the retirement age of taxi drivers to 78 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Of course, older taxi drivers have to go through health checks every year because safety comes first.

sections.label: Removing barriers for seniors
sections.summary: Increasing the retirement and re-employment age further removes barriers and antiquated mindsets of being senior.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The move to increase the retirement and re-employment age, further removes the barriers and antiquated mindsets of being senior.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age changes
sections.summary: Changes to retirement and re-employment age plus CPF tweaks give older workers flexibility and choice, not obligation, to work longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: With changes to the retirement and re-employment age coupled with the tweaks to streamline the CPF system, I look forward to continued employment with more secure retirement outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments give older workers the flexibility and choice, not obligation, to continue working for a longer time if they are willing and able, in line with increases in life expectancy and our ageing population.

sections.label: Re-employment resetting retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: A retrenched worker with 22 years' service was paid as having served two years because the re-employment contract reset retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When COVID-19 forced the company to undertake a retrenchment exercise, like her colleagues, she felt anxious.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But that anxiety turned into dismay when she learnt that her retrenchment payouts considered her not as an employee who had served for 22 years as she had, but as an employee who had served for two years, because the re-employment contract reset the clock on retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Having deemed that a given employee continues to be able to contribute to the organisation by offering re-employment, is it not unfair for retrenchment benefits not to recognise his/her full length of service, especially if nothing else has changed in their roles, but even if the roles have been adjusted a bit?

sections.label: Faster payouts for families
sections.summary: The proposed amendments would let more families receive payouts sooner during a difficult time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments would allow more families to receive payouts sooner, during a difficult time.

sections.label: Contacting overseas Singaporean family members
sections.summary: The member asks what efforts are made to contact and facilitate disbursements to overseas Singaporean family members, whether nominated or un-nominated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Regardless of whether they are named as nominees or the account is un-nominated, what efforts are made to contact and facilitate disbursements to Singaporean family members who are overseas, which is now not an insignificant number, especially in light of continued travel restrictions that may make it difficult for them to come back to settle the affairs?

sections.label: Two changes to the Act
sections.summary: The member welcomes two changes: minimising disruption of the Retirement Account via auto top-up, and simplifying the Act's language.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The proposed amendment follows closely to this matter and I welcome two main changes to this Act: first, minimising disruption of the Retirement Account with the use of auto top-up; second, the simplification of the language of the Act to inch it closer towards the common everyday person.

sections.label: New definition of significant conditions
sections.summary: The member is concerned with the new definition of "significant conditions" for section 15 and new section 15AA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More specifically, I am concerned with the new definition of "significant conditions" in inclusion for the purposes of section 15 and the new section 15AA.

sections.label: Confirming broader significant condition criteria
sections.summary: The member asks the Minister to confirm the new "significant condition" criteria is broader and includes those previously counted under incapacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On this matter, it would be ideal if the Minister can confirm that the new criteria of "significant condition" is broader and includes those previously counted under incapacity.

sections.label: Risk of feeling insignificant
sections.summary: Changing the language to "significance" may mislead a rejected applicant to believe the Board thinks their condition insignificant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: By changing the language to turn this into a matter of "significance", someone rejected in their application for withdrawal may be misled to believe that the Board and, by extension, the Government, think their condition "insignificant".

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age changes
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes impending changes to statutory retirement and re-employment ages, adapting to changing demographics per Tripartite Workgroup recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a world where seniors begin to comprise a growing proportion of society as people live longer and healthier lives, the continued success of our country hinges on the ability to leverage on the experience and expertise of our older countrymen and women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is why the Labour Movement welcomes the impending changes to the statutory limits for the prescribed minimum retirement and re-employment ages, as the Government looks to adapt to our changing demographics in accordance with the recommendations by the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers.

sections.label: RRA protects older workers
sections.summary: RRA protects eager workers from early retirement, gives job security and lets businesses tap experienced workers, though unfair displacement before retirement age may undermine it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Lucy believes that her continued journey in the workforce not only allows her to be independent, but also empowers her with a sense of self-worth has she is still able to contribute actively to society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that the RRA remains relevant, as these age requirements serve not to determine the retirement age of Singaporeans, but to protect eager workers from being retired earlier without taking away their choice as to when they wish to stop working.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the ongoing pandemic undoubtedly has depleted the life savings for some and the guarantee of employment for our senior employees provides a longer runway to build up their nest egg once again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, the changes to the statutory limits to increase the RRA thus is a welcomed move as we look to protect our older Singaporeans who desire to work as it gives them a greater sense of job security and clarity while also providing I would say, businesses the opportunity to continue to tap on a pool of experienced workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet, raising the statutory retirement and re-employment ages may not be meaningful if senior workers are unfairly displaced even before they reach retirement age.

sections.label: Midlife reskilling and career guidance
sections.summary: The speaker calls on Government to give greater career guidance support to older workers, since midlife reskilling and upskilling is a consistent feature of longer lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Learning does not cease in our teens or early 20s, and as we have longer lifespans, our society must reconcile with the notion that midlife reskilling and upskilling is not merely a passing phenomenon, but a consistent feature in our 100-year lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As such, if reskilling and upskilling is to be a mainstay in our workplaces, then I call on the Government to provide greater support and leadership in providing greater and better career guidance to our older workers in order to extend their work life lifespan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Although the Government has provided various avenues through SkillsFuture Singapore and others, more can be done to engage mature workers in their career plans and provide counsel for those navigating these uncharted waters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If we are to extend the productive years of our seniors, we must look to increase the employability of our seniors and provide them with the proper job fits.

sections.label: Workgroup recommendations on ages and CPF
sections.summary: The workgroup proposed raising retirement and re-employment ages progressively from 2022 and not later than 2030, and raising CPF contribution rates for older workers aged 55 to 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From their studies, the workgroup then proposed several recommendations prior to raising the retirement and re-employment ages progressively starting in 2022 and not later than 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, they also recommended that CPF contribution rates for our older workers from age 55 to 70 have to be raised accordingly.

sections.label: Senior Worker Support Package and grant
sections.summary: Measures such as the Senior Worker Support Package and the Early Adopter Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Measures such as Senior Worker Support Package and the Early Adopter Grant.

sections.label: Enhancing grants for early adopters
sections.summary: The speaker hopes grant terms can be further enhanced to encourage more employers to be early adopters and not wait till 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hopefully, such grants terms can be further enhanced to encourage more employers be early adopters and not wait till 2030.

sections.label: CPF LIFE payout timing appeal
sections.summary: A member hopes the Government will allow earlier CPF LIFE payouts when workers retire, and notes over two in five CPF members had made nominations by 1 February 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On this ground, I hope the Government can be flexible to allow CPF LIFE payout to be earlier at the time when the worker decides to retire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am also aware that more Singaporeans are even topping up their CPF to earn better interests and payout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, not many are fortunate to be in this condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hopefully, the Government can consider this appeal for our workers to enjoy their retirement years with a steady income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since last year, CPF members have been able to log in to the CPF portal and nominate their beneficiaries using Singpass.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Earlier in February this year, the Minister had, in response to my written Parliamentary Question, shared that more than two in five CPF members have made a nomination as of 1 February 2021.

sections.label: Faster un-nominated CPF payouts
sections.summary: The Public Trustee typically disburses un-nominated CPF monies within four weeks, and the Bill aims for faster payouts to a beneficiary representative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Furthermore, I understand that the PTO will then typically disburse the un-nominated CPF monies within four weeks after the eligible beneficiaries submit the required documents and pay an administrative fee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am therefore glad to learn that one of the amendments brought about from this amendment Bill aims to achieve more expeditious payouts by allowing the PTO to disburse un-nominated CPF monies to a beneficiary representative.

sections.label: Automatic payout after CPF nomination
sections.summary: A member hopes the Ministry will revise SOPs so the CPF Board automatically notifies and pays $10,000 upfront to nominees via PayNow after a nominator's death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Making life easier for a deceased's loved ones should be approached as a practical pushing factor for one to make their CPF nominations during their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry can look into revising the existing SOPs such that upon the passing of those who have made their CPF nomination, the CPF Board will automatically trigger a notification and an immediate upfront payout of $10,000 will be transferred to the nominee via PayNow to the nominee's bank account.

sections.label: CPF nomination reminders after divorce
sections.summary: A member suggests reminding CPF members to review nominations after divorce or a beneficiary's death, and supports the amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am assuming that the CPF Board's rationale could be that the nominations made during the marriage may have been meant to benefit the children from the marriage and thus, need not be automatically revoked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But to avoid such unnecessary controversial family disputes from arising between the estate of the deceased with the nominated beneficiary, perhaps the Ministry can consider adopting the same approach by sending a notification to a member upon their divorce to remind them about a possible need to consider making a new nomination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Many Singaporeans may not know that CPF nominations made before marriage will lapse immediately after marriage, but nominations made after marriage will not lapse after divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the event of a divorce or loss of family members, people often feel helpless and forget the need to amend their CPF nominations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that the relevant authorities can consider giving a gentle reminder to CPF members upon knowing that their nominated beneficiaries are divorced or have passed away, to consider nullifying their previous nominations and make a new nomination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Deputy Speaker, notwithstanding my requests for clarification and suggestions, I stand in support of this amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will offer more protection to older workers who are able to and want to continue working, whether it is for financial reasons or to remain meaningfully engaged in the economy and community.

sections.label: CPF rates for senior workers
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers recommends raising CPF contribution rates for senior workers aged above 55 to 70, and CPF Act changes ease savings and payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers' recommendations is the raising of CPF contribution rates for senior workers aged above 55 to 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will certainly help with providing greater assurance of retirement adequacy, as will the changes to the CPF Act, which will make it easier for members to build up their CPF savings and receive retirement payouts.

sections.label: Workers not covered by CPF
sections.summary: The passage asks how many workers in related industries are currently not covered by CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, how many workers in related industries are currently not covered by CPF?

sections.label: CPF Amendment Bill support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Central Provident Fund (Amendment) Bill, which grants greater flexibility in CPF rules and simplifies CPF processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It affects Singaporeans in a direct and tangible way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support the Central Provident Fund (Amendment) Bill, which grants greater flexibility in CPF rules and simplifies various CPF processes.

sections.label: Withdrawals for significant condition
sections.summary: New section 15AA allows members under 55 who suffer from a significant condition to make withdrawals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 15AA allows withdrawals to be made by members who have not reached 55 years of age but are suffering from a significant condition.

sections.label: Funeral expense reimbursement
sections.summary: The second clarification concerns reimbursement of funeral expenses on the death of a member with no CPF nomination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second clarification relates to the reimbursement of funeral expenses on the death of a member with no CPF nomination.

sections.label: Refund of Retirement Account top-ups
sections.summary: The third clarification concerns the option to apply for a refund of money transferred to top up Retirement Accounts before 1 November 2008.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My third clarification relates to the option to apply for a refund of money transferred to top up Retirement Accounts before 1 November 2008.

sections.label: Discrimination against senior volunteers
sections.summary: The speaker emphasises not discriminating against seniors in volunteer roles, notes the stand against age discrimination at workplaces, and proposes raising retirement and re-employment ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Specifically, I would like to emphasise the importance of not discriminating against seniors who serve in volunteer roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have made a strong stand on discrimination at workplaces based on age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are now proposing to increase the retirement and re-employment ages to give people the opportunity to work longer.

sections.label: Leadership tenure based on time
sections.summary: The speaker says seniors should be given opportunities to serve an appropriate amount of time and that leadership tenure restrictions should be based on time served, not age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They should be given the opportunities to serve for an appropriate amount of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I do agree in leadership renewal but restrictions on leadership tenure should be based on time served and not age.

sections.label: Senior volunteers discrimination stand
sections.summary: The passage says senior volunteers should not be discriminated against and a strong stand should be taken on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the same spirit of this Bill, senior volunteers should not be discriminated against and we should similarly take a strong stand on this.

sections.label: Jobs matching older workers
sections.summary: It states such jobs match skill sets, experiences or interests, and notes the employment rate of those aged 65 and above rose from 27.6% in 2019 to 28.5% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These would be jobs that match their skill sets, experiences or interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is heartening to note that the employment rate of those aged 65 and above has increased from 27.6% in 2019 to 28.5% in 2020 despite a pandemic-ravaged economy.

sections.label: Retirement-age employees not re-employed
sections.summary: The passage states many employees who reached retirement age are not re-employed, and others were constructively dismissed by employers who reduced working hours, responsibilities, salary and benefits without prior consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: From my conversations on the ground, I understand that many employees who have reach the retirement age are actually not re-employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Others were constructively dismissed by employers who deliberately reduce their working hours, responsibilities and consequently, their salary and benefits without prior consultation.

sections.label: Retirement age rise deferred
sections.summary: The passage states the decision to raise the retirement age to 63 was deferred once because of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The decision to raise the retirement age to 63 was deferred once because of COVID-19.

sections.label: Flexible re-employment options support
sections.summary: It says some are no longer fit for long hours but still willing to contribute, and workforce transformation should encourage job-sharing and flexible working hours as re-employment options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Others may no longer be fit to work long hours at a stretch, but are still willing to contribute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We should capitalise on workforce transformation to encourage and support employees who have job-sharing and flexible working hours as part of their re-employment options.

sections.label: Job redesign and inclusiveness
sections.summary: The passage states this will increase job inclusiveness so work can be done with reduced risks and lower physical or mental demands, and notes job redesign is among the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This will increase job inclusiveness, so they can be done with reduced risks and lower demands physically or mentally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that redesigning jobs at the workplace is among the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers recommendations.

sections.label: Retirement age and CPF payouts
sections.summary: Senior residents worry that raising the retirement age will also raise the CPF withdrawal and Silver Support eligibility ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Many of my senior residents are concerned about the impact of raising the retirement age on CPF payouts and Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They worry that if the retirement age was to go up further, so, too, will the CPF withdrawal age and Silver Support Scheme eligibility age.

sections.label: Plans to achieve BRS
sections.summary: It asks what plans the Government has to help lower-income Singaporeans achieve the BRS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, what are the Government’s plans to assist lower-income Singaporeans to achieve the BRS?

sections.label: Retirement and Re-employment Amendment Bill
sections.summary: It affirms MOM's Bill setting the minimum retirement age at 65 and re-employment age from 67 to 70, citing 25.7% of the labour force aged 55 and older in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Retirement should not become a problem but, rather, a milestone to look forward to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would first like to start by affirming the efforts of MOM in introducing the Retirement and Re-employment (Amendment) Bill to prohibit dismissal of employees on the grounds of age by legislating the minimum retirement age at 65 and increasing the statutory limits for re-employment age from 67 to 70 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to MOM’s Comprehensive Labour Force Survey, as of 2020, 25.7% of our labour force is 55 and older.

sections.label: Chronic illness and older workers
sections.summary: It cites a study showing more chronic conditions and asks what safeguards stop chronic illnesses from unfairly marking older workers as not medically fit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The "Transitions in Health, Employment, Social Engagement and Intergenerational Transfers in Singapore" study showed that, in 2017, around 37% of respondents reported three or more chronic health conditions, up from 19.8% in a 2009 study.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although subsection (2) of the Bill states that the employers have to prove on a balance of probabilities that the employee is not medically fit, I would like to clarify what are the safeguards to assure that chronic illnesses would not be used to unfairly disadvantage older workers from being regarded as medically fit.

sections.label: MediSave contributions and beneficiary representatives
sections.summary: It asks whether excess MediSave voluntary contributions can be reallocated to the Retirement Account, and how beneficiary representatives are identified and remaining beneficiaries protected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is understandable that individuals who have made excess voluntary contributions to their MediSave account during their productive work life, but do not have much health issues or incur much medical costs, would want to use that money for their retirement living expenses instead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to clarify if after lifting the CPF annual limits for voluntary contributions made to the MediSave account, will CPF Board also allow CPF members to reallocate their additional voluntary contributions into other accounts, such as their Retirement Account (RA), if they so choose to in the future?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lastly, the amendment Bill also provides for a new and simplified process for the distribution of un-nominated CPF monies by the Public Trustee on a member's death to a "beneficiary representative" for distribution to the beneficiaries, in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act or section 112 of the Administration of Muslim Law Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although the application will be subject to the approval of the Public Trustee, I am concerned that there is a lack of recourse if the beneficiary representative fails to exercise fairness in distribution of the CPF monies according to the Acts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am also concerned that the beneficiary representative may unreasonably withhold the monies from some beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to seek clarification on: one, how the application process will be done to identify the beneficiary representative and two, how the Public Trustee intends to ensure that the welfare of the remaining beneficiaries will be taken care of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to MOH's action plan for successful ageing, about 25% of our population will be over 65 by 2030 and the United Nations projects this percentage to be almost one in two by 2050.

sections.label: Employment assistance payment for senior employees
sections.summary: It states that companies unable to retain senior employees or find alternatives may offer a one-off employment assistance payment of 3.5 months' salary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Companies that are unable to retain their senior employees or find alternatives, may offer a one-off employment assistance payment, with the recommended sum being 3.5 months worth of salary.

sections.label: Re-employment of retrenched residents 60+
sections.summary: 43.8% of retrenched residents aged 60 and above re-entered re-employment six months post-retrenchment in the second quarter of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The proportion of retrenched residents aged 60 and above who re-entered re-employment six months post-retrenchment, is 43.8% for the second quarter of 2021.

sections.label: TAFEP ageism complaints share
sections.summary: TAFEP's 2020 to 2021 annual report showed the proportion of ageism-related complaints rose to about 12.5%, higher than the 10% the year before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: TAFEP's annual report for the annual year 2020 to 2021, showed that the proportion of complaints related to ageism rose to about 12.5% higher than the 10% reported in the year before.

sections.label: Wage offsets for older workers
sections.summary: The CPF Transition Offset, Senior Employment Credit and Senior Worker Early Adoption Grant support progressive employers; the Senior Employment Credit expires end of next year, and extensions are asked about.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The CPF Transition Offset, Senior Employment Credit scheme, as well as the Senior Worker Early Adoption Grant have all been helpful in supporting progressive employers in maintaining older workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Senior Employment Credit scheme is also set to expire at the end of next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider extending some form of wage offset scheme to support firms to increase their re-employment age policies along with the increase in the statutory cap?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider extending further assistance to employers who are specifically supporting workers over 70 who choose to work, instead of only supporting based on internal retirement and re-employment ages?

sections.label: CPF step-down age and vocational maps
sections.summary: Suggestions are to accelerate the CPF contribution step-down age from 55 to 60 and develop vocational transformation maps with ITMs, with the step-down principle called sound.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, is to accelerate the changes of the age from which the step-down model of CPF contribution rates takes place from 55 to 60; second, is to accelerate the development of vocational transformation maps along with Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The core principle of the CPF contribution rate remains sound and that lowering it at a specific age encourages our employers to continue finding hiring older workers attractive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Government had accepted the recommendation by the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers to start the CPF step-down rate at age 60.

sections.label: Vocational transformation maps as horizontals
sections.summary: Because ITMs are scoped by sectors or verticals, more horizontals in the form of vocational transformation maps need to be introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As ITMs are scoped based on sectors/verticals, we need to introduce more horizontals in the form of vocational transformation maps.

sections.label: Empowering senior workers, two suggestions
sections.summary: Senior workers with credible vocational experience can translate skills to digital and green economy areas, and two suggestions are made to reframe Singapore's workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In this way, we can empower as many senior workers as possible who have credible experience in a vocation to translate their skills and experience to new areas of applications in the digital and green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will also consider my two suggestions: (a) to accelerate the changes of the age from which CPF contribution rates step down from 55 to 60; and (b) to accelerate the development of vocational transformation maps along with ITMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We have the opportunity now to reframe our workforce composition for the future and move Singapore into being a competitive and inclusive talent capital.

sections.label: Retirement and Re-employment Bill
sections.summary: The Bill lets seniors who wish to keep working do so and lets businesses tap experienced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Retirement and Re-employment Bill enables seniors who wish to continue working to do so, allowing them to stay active and contribute to our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Bill will also enable businesses to tap on this experienced pool of workers.

sections.label: Unfair re-employment contracts
sections.summary: Some felt they had unfair re-employment contracts with the same job scope but lower remuneration or benefits, so legislation is needed for fair treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Some also highlight that they were subjected, or they felt that they had unfair re-employment contracts as they were offered re-employment with the same job scope while receiving a lower remuneration or benefits package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, to meet the intent of the extension of the re-employment and retirement age, this amendment must be accompanied by legislation to ensure fair treatment for our senior workers.

sections.label: Age and job suitability
sections.summary: Age should not assess workers' suitability for any job, so extending re-employment and retirement age must come with employers developing retirement and training plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There should not be a case where age is used to assess the workers’ suitability for any job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, it is crucial that the extension of re-employment and retirement age must be accompanied by employers spending time developing a retirement and training plan for our maturing workers.

sections.label: Job redesign company uptake
sections.summary: The passage asks how more companies can be brought on board for job redesign and whether the Ministry has sufficient resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Though there are many job redesign initiatives in various industries, such as in cleaning and retail, how do we get more companies on board?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Of the half million business entities in Singapore, how many are actively looking at job redesign to hire more workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that job redesign takes a lot of effort and guidance, does the Ministry have sufficient resources devoted to this end?

sections.label: Fair employment practices course
sections.summary: The passage asks whether HR practitioners of organisations with more than one employee could be required to attend a fair employment practices course and designate a champion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider requiring all HR practitioners of organisations having more than one employee to attend a course on understanding fair employment practices before they are allowed to recruit employees and designate at least one employee of the organisation as a fair employment practices champion, similar to what we have for safety at the workplace?

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: The passage supports gradually raising the retirement age from 62 to 63 and re-employment age from 67 to 68, reaching 65 and 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
