sentences.text: Older workers have a wealth of experience which they can tap upon to continue contributing to our economy, as well as wisdom and insight, to share with younger cohorts in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support the proposal to increase the retirement age and re-employment age gradually, from 62 to 63 years and from 67 to 68 years respectively from next July, to eventually reach 65 and 70 years by 2030.

sections.label: Concern on non-refundable top-ups
sections.summary: The speaker has a concern about the amendment treating top-ups to Retirement or Special Accounts as non-refundable gifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last, I have a concern regarding the amendment to treat top-ups to members' Retirement Accounts or Special Accounts as non-refundable gifts.

sections.label: Children deterred from topping up parents
sections.summary: Some children may be deterred from topping up parents' accounts, affecting elderly women with less CPF savings who tend to outlive husbands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Some children may be deterred from topping up their parents' accounts and the impact may be felt more among elderly women who have less CPF savings in the first place and tend to outlive their husbands.

sections.label: Future top-ups not refundable
sections.summary: Under the amendment, future top-ups will not be refundable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the amendment, future top-ups will not be refundable.

sections.label: Public Trustee disbursing un-nominated CPF
sections.summary: The speaker notes plans to allow the Public Trustee to disburse un-nominated CPF monies to a beneficiary representative on a member's death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, I note that there are plans to allow the Public Trustee to disburse un-nominated CPF monies to a beneficiary representative on a member’s death.

sections.label: Clarify abolishing Retirement Sum refunds
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government can clarify the amendment abolishing refunds of Retirement Sum top-ups to the giver in any event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, can the Government clarify the amendment to abolish refunds of Retirement Sum top-ups to the giver in any event?

sections.label: Time to return CPF monies
sections.summary: The speaker asks how long it would normally take for CPF monies to be returned to the beneficiary after the member's death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Fourth, how long would it normally take for the CPF monies to be returned to the beneficiary when the CPF member has passed away?

sections.label: Mercer index sustainability rating
sections.summary: The passage states that the weakest link in the Mercer Global Performance Index is the sustainability of the system, rated 59.9 out of 100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Circling back to our performance on the Mercer Global Performance Index, our weakest link is the sustainability of the system, which was given a rating of 59.9 out of 100.

sections.label: CPF withdrawal age and flexibility
sections.summary: The passage says changes to the withdrawal age should be deliberated, and supports CPF Act amendments allowing more flexibility and simplified processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Naturally, any change to the withdrawal age should be done with great deliberation, without discounting the concerns of those who worry that they will not be able to leverage their CPF savings in times of crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps, improving flexibility of withdrawals in tandem would help to alleviate such concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Minister Tan See Leng, in his opening speech, had highlighted that amendments to the CPF Act aims to allow more flexibility and to simplify the CPF processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am supportive of the move to keep it simple and focused on the retirement objectives.

sections.label: Specified limit and BR claims
sections.summary: The passage states the specified limit aims to simplify beneficiaries' claims of un-nominated CPF monies via the BR and mitigate disagreement or conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Ms He Ting Ru sought clarifications on the specified limit and how it will be determined; and whether it may be changed over time.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It is, as I have mentioned earlier, to simplify and make easier to facilitate the beneficiaries’ claim through the distribution of un-nominated CPF monies via the BR; and also to facilitate the beneficiaries, the speed at which it can be done, while at the same time managing and mitigating the risk of disagreement or conflict which might arise between the beneficiaries.

sections.label: How a BR is identified
sections.summary: The passage states that a BR is not pre-identified by the Public Trustee's Office, answering questions on identification and eligibility.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To answer Ms Ng Ling Ling’s question on how a BR is identified and also Mr Saktiandi Supaat’s question on who is eligible to be a BR, let me first explain that a BR is not “pre-identified” by the Public Trustee's Office (PTO).

sections.label: BR consent and beneficiary welfare
sections.summary: The passage states a BR applicant must declare being sole beneficiary or having obtained consent of all other eligible beneficiaries, which the PTO confirms before payout.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This addresses Ms Ng Ling Ling’s question on how the Public Trustee intends to ensure that the welfare of eligible beneficiaries will be taken care of.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It will be a requirement of the application process for the BR that the eligible beneficiary applying to be the BR must declare that he or she is either the sole beneficiary, or that he or she has obtained the consent of all the other eligible beneficiaries which the BR is seeking to represent in making the claim.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The PTO will then confirm with the other eligible beneficiaries directly that they have given their consent, before the PTO pays out any un-nominated funds, CPF monies, to the BR for the BR’s onward distribution to the other beneficiaries.

sections.label: Specified limit set at $10,000
sections.summary: The passage states that the specified limit will be set at $10,000, as Minister Tan See Leng earlier mentioned.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms He Ting Ru’s questions on the specified limit, I think Minister Tan See Leng earlier mentioned that the specified limit will be set at $10,000.

sections.label: Specified limit for un-nominated claims
sections.summary: A $10,000 limit would let about half of current cases claim un-nominated sums, many uncontentious and suited to an expedited scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: A specified limit of $10,000 would allow around half of the current number of cases coming forward to make a claim for un-nominated sums and we believe that, of this half, a substantial number will be uncontentious and will benefit from an expedited scheme like this.

sections.label: Faster disbursement of un-nominated monies
sections.summary: Un-nominated CPF monies could be disbursed to the BR about two weeks after application approval, faster than the standard claim process.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In our estimation, the un-nominated CPF monies under this scheme could be disbursed to the BR within about two weeks from the approval of the application, as compared to a much longer period of time under the current standard claim process.

sections.label: Electronic payment to overseas accounts
sections.summary: Payments will be disbursed electronically by telegraphic transfer, demand draft or other methods to overseas accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Payments will also be disbursed electronically via telegraphic transfers or demand drafts if they prefer, or whichever other method, to their overseas account.

sections.label: Funeral expense reimbursement from CPF monies
sections.summary: Funeral expense reimbursement from un-nominated CPF monies is capped at $6,000 and payable only to eligible beneficiaries with consent and receipts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The reimbursement of funeral expenses out of a deceased member’s un-nominated CPF monies is capped at $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Eligible beneficiaries who intend to claim for the reimbursement of funeral expenses from the deceased CPF members’ un-nominated CPF monies may do so by submitting the relevant Funeral Reimbursement Form, with the appropriate supporting receipts and so on, after obtaining consent from the rest of the beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the CPF Act, the Public Trustee has the duty to distribute un-nominated CPF monies only to eligible beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: By extension, reimbursements for funeral expenses can only, therefore, be made to eligible beneficiaries and not to a wider pool, beyond what the statute provides.

sections.label: Dispute resolution and locating beneficiaries
sections.summary: Without agreement the standard claims process applies, and the PTO is asked to consider mediation and PayNow for locating beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If they are unable to reach agreement, then the current standard claims process will apply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to check whether the PTO can consider offering an alternate dispute resolution process, for example, through a mediation, when parties are unable to identify and agree on a representative so that the matter can still be processed expeditiously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The second one is locating the beneficiaries, whether the PTO would consider perhaps, to find out whether the beneficiaries have any PayNow accounts and actually explore for the funds to be transferred through that manner.

sections.label: PayNow as electronic payment option
sections.summary: The Member's PayNow suggestion will be considered alongside other electronic payment platform options as viable alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the Member's suggestion on PayNow, obviously, given the range of different electronic options I have outlined earlier, we will certainly consider PayNow or any other electronic payment platform options as viable alternatives.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age increase
sections.summary: The plan to raise the retirement age to 65 and re-employment age to 70 by the end of the decade is ambitious but achievable, with the first increase on 1 July 2022 on schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The plan to raise the retirement age and re-employment age to 65 and 70 respectively by the end of this decade is ambitious, but it is achievable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The first increase will take place on 1 July 2022 and it is on schedule.

sections.label: Tripartite partners agree on age increases
sections.summary: After consulting stakeholders, tripartite partners agreed to continue the strategy and raise the re-employment age to 70, beyond raising the retirement age to 65 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: After consultation with stakeholders, the tripartite partners have agreed to continue with this strategy and, beyond raising the retirement age to 65 by 2030, they have also agreed to raise the re-employment age to 70.

sections.label: Guidelines on re-employing older employees
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines on the Re-employment of Older Employees state that employers should engage employees at least six months before they reach retirement age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines on the Re-employment of Older Employees make clear that employers should engage employees at least six months before they reach retirement age.

sections.label: Re-employed workers' wages and benefits
sections.summary: More than 95% of workers re-employed in the same job did not experience any cuts to their wages and benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: More than 95% of workers re-employed in the same job did not experience any cuts to their wages and benefits.

sections.label: Increase in EAP amounts
sections.summary: The tripartite partners agreed to increase the minimum and maximum EAP amounts from 1 July 2022 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, the tripartite partners agreed to increase the minimum and maximum EAP amounts from 1 July 2022 onwards.

sections.label: Workplace fairness legislation deliberations
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness is deliberating the scope of legislation on workplace discrimination and hopes to finalise recommendations by the first half of 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As Members have noted in their speeches, the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness, which I co-chair, is deliberating on the scope of legislation to address workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are making progress in the discussions and we hope to finalise our recommendations by the first half of 2022.

sections.label: CPF Act amendments and withdrawals
sections.summary: Proposed CPF Act amendments will not change rules for CPF lump sum withdrawals or schemes like Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, in response to points made by Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Gan Thiam Poh, let me reiterate that the proposed amendments to the CPF Act will not change the rules for CPF lump sum withdrawals or other social support schemes like Silver Support.

sections.label: Deferring after 65
sections.summary: For every year deferred after 65, the increase could be up to 7% more per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In fact, yesterday, I shared that for every year that they defer after 65, the increase could be up to 7% more per annum.

sections.label: Early CPF withdrawal conditions
sections.summary: Members with conditions can qualify for early CPF withdrawal if certified as having reduced life expectancy, being permanently unfit to work, or lacking mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Today, Members with conditions of any kind, including auto-immune or neurological diseases, can qualify for early withdrawal of CPF savings if they are certified by a doctor as having a reduced life expectancy or being permanently unfit to work, or lacking mental capacity.

sections.label: CPF Board and nominees
sections.summary: CPF Board reaches out to nominees, including overseas, once notified of a member's death and disburses monies within a month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: CPF Board already reaches out to nominees, including those overseas, once it is notified of a member's death and it disburses the monies within a month, having allowed time for medical institutions to deduct any medical bills from the deceased member's MediSave Account.

sections.label: CPF Transition Offset
sections.summary: The Government will support employers through the CPF Transition Offset, implemented on 1 January 2022 as part of the Senior Worker Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government will support employers through the CPF Transition Offset, which Mr Heng Chee How, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin have all touched on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This will be implemented on 1 January 2022 as part of the Senior Worker Support Package.

sections.label: Progress on senior worker employment
sections.summary: The Government will continue to simplify rules and improve communications to CPF members to build a more inclusive economy and society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are confident that further progress on senior worker employment will be made.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will continue to simplify rules; we will continue to improve communications to our CPF members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With the support of Members of the House, businesses, unions and, most importantly, fellow Singaporeans, we will be a more inclusive economy and society.

sections.label: Age-based dismissal and MOM appeals
sections.summary: It states companies should not deny jobs to those near statutory retirement age and allows age-dismissed employees to appeal to MOM.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At the point of the recruitment, particularly when his tenure, based on the fixed contract, has expired and if he is looking for a job, and if, say, it is within three to five years of the statutory retirement age, no company should deprive him of the opportunity of being employed because of the fact that he is near the statutory retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On top of that, if an employee has been dismissed on grounds of age, and if they believe so, this retirement age allows the employee to appeal to MOM to look into it and to investigate whether there were grounds.

sections.label: CPF withdrawal and Retirement Account
sections.summary: It states a member at 55 can withdraw $5,000 from CPF and is expected to have the Basic Retirement Sum in the Retirement Account.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At 55, the member can withdraw a guaranteed sum of $ 5,000, provided he has the money in his CPF account.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In the Retirement Account, he is expected to have the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS), which I believe is pegged at $93,000 today.
